definitions.explanation: Whether a business, project, or investment yields enough revenue to cover costs and produce a profit.

examples.japanese: {採算|さいさん}が{取|と}れない。
{採算|さいさん}を{度外視|どがいし}してでも、このサービスを{続|つづ}けたい。
examples.english: I want to continue this service even if we ignore profitability.

examples.japanese: {過疎|かそ}{地域|ちいき}の{路線|ろせん}バスは{採算|さいさん}が{合|あ}わず、{廃止|はいし}される{路線|ろせん}が{増|ふ}えている。
examples.english: Bus routes in depopulated areas are unprofitable, and the number of discontinued routes is increasing.

notes:
WORD FORMATION:
{採|さい} (take, gather) + {算|さん} (calculate) = calculating the take (i.e., whether the numbers work out).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {採算|さいさん}が{取|と}れる: to be profitable
- {採算|さいさん}が{合|あ}う: to be cost-effective
- {採算|さいさん}が{合|あ}わない: to be unprofitable
- {採算|さいさん}を{度外視|どがいし}する: to disregard profitability
- {採算|さいさん}{割|わ}れ: running at a loss
- {採算|さいさん}ライン: break-even point

USAGE NOTE:
{採算|さいさん} is a business term. The most common patterns are {採算|さいさん}が{取|と}れる/{取|と}れない (profitable/unprofitable) and {採算|さいさん}が{合|あ}う/{合|あ}わない (cost-effective/not cost-effective).
